Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Consumer Goods third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question, and instructions will follow. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.  

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Consumer Goods' third quarter results. With me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ruiz, Chief Marketing Officer; Karen Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Innovation Officer; Emily Wong, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Thompson.  

Mike Thompson:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Apex Consumer Goods delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Today, our discussion will touch on our overall financial performance, including robust organic sales growth and gross margin expansion; the strength across our key brands and categories; supply chain efficiencies; marketing initiatives; sustainability efforts; digital advancements; sales and channel strategies; and our outlook for the rest of the year.  

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Lisa Chen:  
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.5 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year. On an organic basis, sales grew 5.1%, ahead of our expectations and outpacing the broader CPG category. Gross margin was 43.2%, up 180 basis points year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially on an FX-neutral basis. This marks our third consecutive quarter of margin expansion, driven by disciplined execution on commodity costs, pricing, and mix. Operating income was $720 million, and diluted earnings per share were $1.45. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me unpack our gross margin performance in more detail, as it's a key highlight. This quarter's 43.2% gross margin was our strongest in five years, reflecting gains across our Snacks, Beverages, and Household Essentials segments. Commodity costs provided a 120 basis point tailwind, a sharp reversal from the 300-plus basis point drag in the prior year amid peak inflation. We've benefited from stabilization in our input basket, with resolved supply chain issues from the Russia-Ukraine conflict and better weather in growing regions. Cocoa and coffee remain volatile—cocoa up 25% year-to-date due to Ivory Coast constraints, much like what peers have noted—but our forward hedging, covering 85% of 2025 needs at $3,200 per metric ton below spot prices, protected us from 60 basis points of erosion. Coffee futures eased 15% sequentially, helping our ready-to-drink lines. Palm oil dropped 10% quarter-over-quarter from Indonesian production ramps, adding 40 basis points in Household Essentials, while wheat for Snacks fell 8% year-over-year on strong exports, though we're watching Indian bans closely. Sugar, corn, packaging resins, and aluminum also improved modestly. North America saw costs 2% below plan, while EMEA had a slight overrun from natural gas. We're deepening ties with sustainable suppliers like Cargill's Regen10 for palm oil and using AI-driven forecasting in our SAP S/4HANA system to time procurement better. We anticipate 50 to 100 basis points of commodity tailwinds in Q4, barring shocks.  

Pricing was even stronger, contributing 250 basis points of expansion with average selling prices up 5.2% year-over-year. This came from list price hikes, promotional resets, and trade spend optimization, with volume declines limited to 1.5%, aligning with peers. In Snacks, we lifted ASP 6% on core items like Apex Crunch bars using everyday low pricing in mass channels to counter private labels at Walmart and Kroger. Beverages saw 4.5% pricing, boosted by 12% premiumization in electrolytes. Household Essentials took a 4% increase amid Unilever competition in laundry. APAC delivered 7% pricing on urban premium demand in China and India, offsetting softer Latin America. Our consumer testing via NielsenIQ and dynamic CRM tools keeps us ahead of 3-4% category inflation, with net price realization 150 basis points above the CPG average per Circana.  

Mix added 110 basis points from portfolio shifts toward high-margin SKUs, with premium products now 28% of sales, up from 22% two years ago, for 500 basis points uplift. Premium Snacks like organic nuts and plant-based chips grew 15%, shifting mix positively; North America, at 46% margins, hit 55% of sales via e-commerce and DTC; club channels like Costco now 22% of volume with 300 basis points higher margins. Project Elevate pushes protein-fortified snacks launching Q1 2025 at 50% margins, SKU rationalization cut low-margin tail by 12%, and plant automation like Ohio robotic palletizing reduced conversion costs 15%.  

This performance builds on our Q3 organic sales growth of 5.1%, ahead of the industry's 2.1% per NielsenIQ. Volume added 1.2%, pricing 3.4%, mix 0.2%, with 14 sequential actions averaging mid-single digits to offset 7-9% COGS inflation in cocoa, coffee, and palm oil. Premium brands like skincare saw limited volume trade-off, while value Snacks held flat against private labels. We gained 10 basis points North America market share, with plant-based extensions posting 18% velocity in convenience. North America grew 5.5% on Snacks and Beverages; Europe 3.2% pricing-led; APAC and LatAm 6.8% on mini-packs and sachets. Portfolio shaping focused on 10 high-growth platforms, RGM optimized trade spend, and supply chain cut lead times 25%, hedging 80% cocoa at favorable levels.  

Geographically, developed markets at 62% of sales delivered 3% organic growth—North America up 4% on Snacks share gains and 18% e-commerce, Europe flat with sustainable household strength—while emerging markets at 38% surged 18%, led by 22% APAC on urban skincare and 14% LatAm on localized snacks. Emerging drove over 40% of incremental growth, with urbanization and middle-class expansion as tailwinds; we're allocating 55% of capex there, including ASEAN and Brazil hubs.  

By category, Beauty & Personal Care grew 6.8% organically, with Lumina Skincare up 12% on serums and e-commerce; Home Care 2.1% holding share; Nutrition & Refreshment 3.9% on health snacks and hydration. We gained share in 12 of 15 top brands.  

Competitively, we've countered P&G's laundry promotions gaining 120 basis points, PepsiCo's bundling, and private label surges by holding ASP firm, reallocating trade spend via AI platforms for 15% basket uplift, accelerating innovations like protein chips stealing share, pruning SKUs, and expanding DTC/club to 18% of sales. Early Q4 shows us gaining versus category.  

For full-year gross margin, we guide 46.0% to 47.0%, 120 basis points expansion at midpoint from 44.8% prior year. Pricing/mix +200-250 basis points with 7% YTD net pricing; inputs -50-80 basis points at 3-4% inflation, hedged on cocoa/palm; productivity +150-200 from $250 million savings via AI forecasting, aseptic lines, and nearshoring; FX -30 basis points. Q4 at 43-44%, with upper half possible if commodities moderate.  

These results position us strongly. Next, David will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.  

David Ruiz:  
Thank you, Lisa. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across all our channels, especially with our new Live Boldly campaign, which emphasizes premium health-focused products and has driven 12% uplift in consumer awareness per recent Nielsen panels. We've tailored promotions to counter competitive intensity, focusing shopper marketing on high-ROI velocity drivers while advancing sustainability messaging that resonates in both developed and emerging markets.  

Following me, Karen will discuss supply chain performance.  

Karen Patel:  
Thank you, David. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. Our Margin Accelerator program delivered key savings through zero-based budgeting across global plants, AI-optimized inventory reducing waste 18%, high-speed filling lines boosting throughput 25%, and nearshoring cutting freight 15%. We're also focused on reducing our carbon footprint via sustainable sourcing like RSPO palm oil and blockchain traceability, aligning with ESG goals while hedging costs effectively.  

After me, Raj will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.  

Raj Singh:  
Thank you, Karen. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent launch, VitalVeg Protein Snacks, has been well-received by consumers, growing 25% in early distribution with 55% gross margins and capturing share in the better-for-you segment amid wellness trends. This ties into our Project Elevate and precision fermentation efforts for plant-based adjacencies, positioning us for H2 acceleration.  

Finally, Emily will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.  

Emily Wong:  
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving our sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel, now 22% of volume with higher margins, and we are also investing in our retail partnerships like Kroger resets and club exclusives at Costco. Emerging markets expansion added outlets, driving volume in APAC and LatAm.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for questions: Press star one if you have a question. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morningstar.  

Alex Rivera:  
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?  

Raj Singh:  
Great question, Alex. Sustainability is core to our innovation agenda. We've embedded it across 40% of Beauty & Personal Care SKUs with recyclable packaging, boosting loyalty, and advanced Farm-to-Factory blockchain for 60% of cocoa to meet EU deforestation rules. In Home Care, EcoWash captures green subsegments, and overall, initiatives like Regen10 palm oil and recycled PET support our Planet & Society goals while delivering productivity. Consumers reward this—NPS up in eco-lines—and it de-risks supply amid regs.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Barclays.  

Jordan Lee:  
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?  

Emily Wong:  
Thanks, Jordan. Emerging markets are our growth engine, up 18% organically. We're tilting capex 55% there, with a Vietnam ASEAN hub for Snacks and Brazil expansions via localized launches like pão de queijo chips gaining 8 points share. In India, Gujarat facility cuts costs 18%; China e-comm doubles velocity. Distribution to 2.5 million outlets, hyper-local digital activations, and 65% local sourcing mitigate FX—aiming 15-18% growth in FY24.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Taylor Kim with Goldman Sachs.  

Taylor Kim:  
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?  

Lisa Chen:  
Sure, Taylor. Inflation remains sticky but cooling, with our 5.2% ASP up 6.8% organically offsetting 3-4% input rises. Elasticity at -1.2 to -1.5 held volumes to -2.1%, better than feared. We tiered hikes—8.5% Snacks for cocoa, nuanced 6.2% Beverages via AI dynamic pricing reducing trade spend. EM took 9.8% with volume gains; NA conservative at 6.4%. This drove 520 basis points YTD margin expansion, with Q4 +6-7% pricing as inflation moderates.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with JPMorgan.  

Chris Patel:  
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?  

Karen Patel:  
Excellent point, Chris. AI is transformative—Blue Yonder partnership cuts inventory waste 18%, DemandSense optimizes shelf pricing for 15% basket uplift, Nexus reduces forecast error 25%, and SAP ML handles procurement timing. In plants, robotic automation and high-speed lines yield $250 million savings; it's key to our 150-200 basis point productivity and resilience versus port strikes or volatility.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.  

Mike Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.  

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex Consumer Goods third quarter Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
